questions.question: What does expressive intention mean in dance?
choices: The idea, feeling, or quality a performer aims to communicate

questions.question: How can dynamics affect a dance performance?
choices: Changes in force, speed, or flow can shape expressive meaning
They change the music's key automatically

questions.question: What does focus refer to in performance?
choices: Where the dancer directs attention through gaze or body orientation

questions.question: A dancer looks toward a partner during a sequence. What may this communicate?
choices: The music must be in 3/4 time
A relationship or point of attention within the choreography

questions.question: Why is projection useful in performance?
choices: It helps movement and intention read clearly to an audience
It means dancing at maximum force at all times

questions.question: A performer changes a movement from soft and sustained to sharp and percussive. What is being varied?
What is stage presence?
choices: The number of props on stage
A performer's ability to sustain focus and engage the audience

questions.question: A dancer loses timing during rehearsal. What is a constructive next step?
choices: Hide the error and avoid rehearsal
Change the choreography without telling the group
Review counts or musical cues and practice the transition

questions.question: Why should a performer connect facial expression and movement to the dance's intent?
choices: Consistent choices can make the communicated idea clearer
Facial expression must always be dramatic
Movement has no meaning without a smile
The audience can only read faces

questions.question: How can breath support performance?
choices: It can help coordinate movement, phrasing, and stamina

questions.question: A performer exaggerates a gesture so it can be seen from the back of a theater. What is the goal?
choices: Make the movement's shape and intention legible at a distance

questions.question: What should a dancer do if a movement causes sharp pain during rehearsal?
choices: Ask a peer to push farther
Stop and seek appropriate guidance rather than forcing the movement

questions.question: Why is feedback after a performance useful?
choices: It can identify what communicated clearly and what could be developed
It proves the performance was unsuccessful
It must be accepted without discussion

questions.question: A dancer's energy drops before the ending. What can support a more consistent performance?
choices: Use maximum force from the beginning
Plan pacing and practice stamina for the full sequence

questions.question: What is one way to interpret a dance performance?
choices: Use movement choices, structure, music, and context as evidence
Assume every viewer has the same response

questions.question: A performer changes level on a musical accent. What can this create?
choices: A change to the audience's seat
A stronger relationship between movement and sound

questions.question: How can stillness be used in performance?
choices: It can create contrast, focus, or a moment of emphasis
It always means the dance has ended
It prevents an audience from watching

questions.question: Why do dancers practice entrances and exits?
choices: They are not part of the dance
They are part of the performance's timing, focus, and spatial organization

questions.question: A performer uses a gesture that seems unclear to viewers. What can the performer or choreographer consider?
choices: Repeat it more quickly without testing
Clarify the movement's intention or provide context through the surrounding phrase

questions.question: What is a useful post-performance reflection?
choices: Identify one strength and one specific choice to develop next time
